turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Reading aloud to children is one of the simplest things parents can do, and research shows it has many benefits.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The first benefit is vocabulary. Children's books often include words that adults rarely use in everyday conversation, such as gigantic, whisper or meadow. Hearing these words in a story, with pictures and context, helps children understand and remember them. Studies suggest that children who are read to regularly hear many more words before starting school.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Reading aloud also builds attention span. This is the length of time a person can focus on one activity. Following a story from beginning to end requires concentration. With regular practice, children become able to listen for longer periods.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Stories also help children understand emotions and other people. They see characters feel scared, happy or jealous, and they learn how others solve problems.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Another key benefit is emotional connection. Sitting close together with a book creates a warm, calm moment in a busy day. Many children remember these times for the rest of their lives.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Experts suggest making reading interactive. Ask questions like, What do you think will happen next? or How does the bear feel? Let children point at pictures and turn the pages.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And reading aloud does not need to stop when children learn to read alone. Older children also enjoy listening to longer stories that are a little too difficult for them to read by themselves.
